hypothesis: Reweight BPR training examples by recency — positive rows from later training dates get exponentially higher gradient weight (via a `recency_decay` hparam, mean-normalized so decay=0 exactly reproduces the current best) — so the shared embeddings are fit closer to the valid/test-time behavior distribution instead of being dominated equally by 2-week-stale early-train rows, directly addressing the EDA's documented temporal drift in tab/duration/long_view-rate.
reflection: The auxiliary is_like head hit 0.6039 (a real but tiny GAUC-only gain) then overfit past epoch 6, and every capacity/architecture/negative-sampling lever tried so far has landed within noise of 0.6035 — suggesting the plateau isn't about model capacity but about training on a distribution that's already stale relative to eval time (EDA flags monotonic drift in tab share, duration, and long_view rate across train→valid→test), a lever nothing has touched yet.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since recency weighting recalibrates the shared per-user/per-item interaction scores that GAUC directly measures, while nDCG@5's top-5 cutoff is a more indirect downstream consequence of the same score shift.
